What is the output of the following Python code?

```python
s = "PLACEMENT"
print(s[2:6] + s[-1])
```
explanation: Indices: P0 L1 A2 C3 E4 M5 E6 N7 T8. The slice s[2:6] takes indices 2 to 5 (end excluded) = "ACEM". s[-1] is the last character "T". Result: "ACEMT".
The array s is sized from the literal "campus": 6 characters plus the terminating '\0', so sizeof(s) = 7. strlen counts characters before '\0', giving 6. Output: 7 6.

stem:
What will be the output of the following pseudo-code? (Arrays are 0-indexed.)

```
Integer arr[6] = {3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9}
for (i = 1 to 5)
  arr[i] = arr[i] + arr[i - 1]
end for
print arr[5] - arr[2]
```
explanation: Each element becomes a running (prefix) sum: arr = {3, 4, 8, 9, 14, 23}. arr[5] − arr[2] = 23 − 8 = 15.
shortcut: arr[5] − arr[2] = sum of original arr[3..5] = 1 + 5 + 9

What will be the output of the following pseudo-code? (Arrays are 0-indexed.)

```
Integer a[5] = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50}
Integer n = 5
for (k = 1 to 2)
  Integer t = a[n - 1]
  for (i = n - 1 down to 1)
    a[i] = a[i - 1]
  end for
  a[0] = t
end for
print a[0], a[3]
```
explanation: Each outer pass rotates the array right by one: the last element moves to the front. Pass 1: {50, 10, 20, 30, 40}. Pass 2: {40, 50, 10, 20, 30}. So a[0] = 40 and a[3] = 20.
shortcut: Right-rotate by 2: last two elements move to the front

What is the output of the following Python code?

```python
s = "code tests logic"
w = s.split()
r = " ".join(x[::-1] for x in w[::-1])
print(r[3:9])
```
explanation: w[::-1] = ["logic", "tests", "code"]; reversing each word gives "cigol", "stset", "edoc", so r = "cigol stset edoc" (the whole string reversed). Indices 3 to 8: o(3) l(4) space(5) s(6) t(7) s(8), giving "ol sts".
shortcut: Reversing word order and each word = reversing the whole string
